newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo says Swiss Mobutu asset finds are a start.
newsitem.headline: Congo says Swiss Mobutu asset finds are a start.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of Congo's justice minister on Tuesday welcomed the discovery of 4.8 million Swiss francs ($3.4 million) in assets held by former President Mobutu Sese, but said it was only the start.

"We say bravo, it's something, but we know there is much more where that came from and we have to suspect that it is not always in the banks' interests to reveal it," Justice Minister Celestin Lwangi told Reuters in Kinshasa.

The funds discovered by Swiss banks in accounts belonging to Mobutu and his family have been frozen in line with Berne's orders last month, Switzerland's Federal Banking Commission said in a statement.

When Mobutu was toppled by rebels last month, the Swiss government ordered all banks in Switzerland to report if they or their foreign subsidiaries were holding wealth for Mobutu, his family or their associates.

"We also have our own international commission which is investigating the amount removed by Mobutu, and its work continues. We cannot lightly make statements about the amount that may be hidden," Lwangi said.

The new government is Kinshasa has sought legal assistance from Berne in tracking down reports that Mobutu stashed billions of dollars of looted national wealth abroad. In a newspaper interview last week, Lwangi alleged Mobutu had put 11 billion Swiss francs in Switzerland.
"It is not just a matter of finding money in bank accounts, it was also kept in property and company shares, it is hidden in any number of ways," Lwangi said.
